system.summary: Additive/subtractive superencipherment, figure by figure without carrying, of the international synoptic weather code; four generations 1938-1940: fixed additive with group exchange (1938), per-group additives (1938-39), autokey on a substituted first group (Far East 1940), indicator-dependent subtractor (Moscow types 17040...05188, Feb-June 1940), and from June 1940 a 109-figure cycle with an indicator group aaabb in clear (two tables, odd and even days)

prior_solution.where: the Japanese Army Meteorological Department's reports themselves (methods, keys, tables, worked examples)

conditions.human_role: Brice Dudout found the file among the JACAR searches on Japanese intercepts, set the rules (transcribe and freeze the tables before any check, test on the reports' own held-out examples), and settled doubtful figures by targeted visual review (shapes only); AI agents transcribed, checked and wrote up.
models: Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic), agents run by Brice Dudout

solution.what: Method passages of the twelve reports transcribed and translated; four June-July 1940 tables (4,796 figures) and two October grids (218 figures) transcribed cell by cell and frozen.
Every row of each June-July table is a rotation of one 109-figure cycle: 0 disagreements on 4,796 figures, 3 illegible figures restored.

Held-out worked example of 6 July 1940 (image 4; tables on images 6-7): key stream drawn from the transcribed table equals the printed stream and gives back the printed clear text, 60/60 figures; type 17040 example 25/25; Audric's British example of the same system 25/25.
Japanese and English web search: no publication of the Japanese work or of the Moscow tables found; the Soviet system of Feb-June 1940 is described by Audric (2000).

outcome.method_basis: Keys, tables and methods recovered by the Japanese Army Meteorological Department in 1938-1940 and given in its reports; transcribed and checked here.
outcome.fraction_read_source: June-July tables: 4,793 of 4,796 figures certain, 3 restored, 0 unresolved; worked example 60/60 figures.

validation.notes: No key recovered by us and no language read: the keys are Japanese; checked on the reports' own held-out examples (60/60, 25/25) and on Audric's example (25/25).

human_check.passage: 5th additive of 12 Nov 1938; subtractor for cipher 6 of 29 Apr 1940; ten cells of the October 1940 grids
human_check.note: 34135 -> 34235; cipher 6 -> 8 probable (6 possible); ten October cells confirmed as read

credits.note: Japanese reports found, method passages transcribed and translated, key tables transcribed and checked (rotation structure, held-out example)

gaps.item: October 1940 odd-day grid: one figure too many (2 and 5 x13, 4 x11), cell not located
no Soviet enciphered broadcast of 1940 found to test the tables externally (TNA HW 54/4, HW 40/31 not digitised)
